name: pair-skein-mass-bar-parity
description: Answers PR #6820 item 2. The bar-EVEN denominator of the pair Skein mass S_ab(q) = (q mu_a + q^-1 mu_b)/(q^1/2 + q^-1/2) in prf:hadron-half-life item 4 is FORCED, not a sign slip: the bar-odd bridge s would make the mirror of a mass negative, and would make S_ab diverge at q=1 where the corpus requires Q -> 0 and decay to cease.
verdict: (R3) deliberate symmetrising normalisation -- S_ab is a mass, not an amplitude
scope: (b) structural exclusion of the odd bridge IN THIS FORMULA, on two proved invariants (finiteness of the q->1 limit; sign-preservation of a mass under the bar involution). Says nothing about which Skein normalisation is canonical elsewhere -- that is #6820's separate question and is untouched.

checks.name: even_denominator_makes_bar_exchange_constituents
checks.detail: S_ab(1/q) - S_ba(q) = 0.0 at 60 dps -- the bar involution exchanges a and b and preserves the sign, so a mass maps to a mass

checks.name: odd_bridge_makes_the_mirror_of_a_mass_negative
checks.detail: S_ab(1/q) + S_ba(q) = 4.97841e-60, i.e. S_ab(1/q) = -S_ba(q). The mirror of the mass 6.1844009 is -6.1844009. Excluded for a mass.

checks.name: even_denominator_gives_the_arithmetic_mean_at_q_eq_1
checks.detail: S_even -> (mu_a+mu_b)/2 = 0.32; the residual falls linearly with q-1 at all three probe points

checks.name: odd_bridge_DIVERGES_at_q_eq_1_like_one_over_q_minus_one
checks.detail: S_odd matches the analytic pole (mu_a+mu_b)/(q-1) to better than 1% at q-1 = 1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-9. Since f(Q) ~ Q^5, the odd bridge makes the decay RATE diverge at q=1 -- the exact opposite of the corpus's own stated limit (hadron-half-life-fermi.md: 'isobars become degenerate (Q = 0) and beta decay ceases'). This is what makes reading (R2), a sign slip, untenable.

checks.name: even_denominator_gives_S_aa_eq_mu_a_at_q_eq_1
checks.detail: S_aa(1+1e-12) = 0.31 against mu_a = 0.31 -- the self-pair reduces to the constituent mass, as a pair mass must
